newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares drop on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares drop on profit-taking.

text.p: Jordanian stocks fell for the first time in a week on Monday with a spate of profit-taking trimming gains after the market's rebound to highest levels in 11 months over Iraq prospects.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.4 percent to 154.49 points after it soared at the last session on Saturday to its highest level since late February.
The market closed on Sunday, a public holiday marking the Moslem Isra'a and Meraj (Prophet Mohammed's Ascension).
High turnover worth 2.92 million dinars ($4.1 million) was mainly dominated by one large bloc sale in Arab International Investment Education worth 1,315,073 dinars.
Profit-taking was focused on industrials that had been steadily rising since news last month of Iraq's imminent implementation of its oil-for food deal.
Brokers said investor sentiment continues to be buttressed by optimism Jordan will stand to gain from Iraq's oil-for-food deal with traders and industrialists clinching some of its lucrative deals.
Investment analysts say Iraq deals could activate a stagnant industrial sector and improve next year's performance of blue-chip firms whose exports are heavily weighted towards Iraq.

Market activity was held firm by continued demand on key drug and vegetable oil firms, with investors reacting positively to Iraqi Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh comments in Amman on Sunday that Jordanian industry was competitive in coming "oil-for-food" deals.

The two top gainers were companies that sell vegetable oils and detergents. Industrial Commercial Agricultural rose a maximum 5 percent to 2.47 dinars and Jordan Selpho Chemical gained 0.04 dinars to 0.84 dinars.
Another stock that saw some speculative activity unrelated to Iraq was Livestock and Poultry which shed 0.01 dinars, on a 153,503 dinar turnover.
Overall losers outstripped gainers, with 23 stocks falling while only 14 declined. Another 10 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of 45 best-traded shares fell 0.09 percent to 83.48, still 12.59 percent down on last year.
